title: Daily ML direction trading on Bitcoin with a real unseen-period test (Crone, Brophy, Ward)
economic_hypothesis: +86% over Q1-2021 (equal to buy-and-hold) and +12.5% better than buy-and-hold after adding a confidence-based risk rule
entry_rules: go long when the next-day direction classifier predicts up (a binary long/cash rule)
exit_rules: no stop is stated; no target is stated; the position is re-decided every day; the prediction or the risk-tolerance score turning
risk_rules: a risk-tolerance score scales exposure, but the exact mapping was not read; none (24/7)
parameters: the models are trained; hyper-parameters are not frozen in the paper
claimed_period: training periods up to 2019-2020 and an unseen test in Q1-2021
claimed_metrics: about +86% over the three-month test (matching buy-and-hold) and +12.5% relative with the confidence-based rule
transaction_cost_model: no fee or slippage model is mentioned
required_data: on-chain network features plus external market features (paper)
external_code: the paper's own code was not published; a benchmark's code is on GitHub
external_results: the paper read in full: an explicit unseen-period trading test
counter_evidence: the same paper documents that a widely cited benchmark in this literature trained on its own test data and mis-applied PCA — a reminder that this literature's reported numbers need auditing
a three-month test window cannot separate skill from a lucky regime
the project's admission cost is a 23.791 bps round trip, and the source declares no cost model (no fee or slippage model is mentioned)
found in the RFC-035S2 strategy-first search; no local backtest influenced this record

evidence_quality: E2 — the paper read in full: an explicit unseen-period trading test
